action: Verify WinRAR and other tools on your network are the publisher's signed copies; apply application allowlisting and code-signing checks, and alert on memory that is read, write and execute at once and on PNGs with truncated headers.
exec: Trusted programs can be rewritten into malware carriers whose fingerprint changes every run, so hash-based blocking is weak.
plain: Security firm ReversingLabs describes BubbleLoader, malware that edits ordinary programs like WinRAR so they secretly load other malware, and changes its fingerprint every time it runs.

key_findings: BubbleLoader patches a program's entry point and adds two PNG images that hold the hidden code; the second PNG is a fake containing encrypted code.
Known hosts include WinRAR, x64dbg, Windows Media Player, the Firefox launcher and virtiofs.
Earliest samples date from February 2026; two activity clusters in mid-September and early October indicate current use.
Runtime polymorphism makes the in-memory payload hash differ on every execution.
ReversingLabs does not say how the tampered programs reach victims (Help Net Security); the final payload varies.
recommendations: Strict application allowlisting and code-signing verification.
Alert on RWX memory and protection changes to ntdll exception routines; flag PNGs with truncated headers.

summary: ReversingLabs analysed BubbleLoader, a loader that rewrites a few instructions at a program's entry point and adds two PNG images to turn legitimate software, including WinRAR and Windows Media Player, into a carrier for other malware. It changes its payload's in-memory hash on every run. Samples date from February 2026, with activity clusters in September and October. Delivery method is not stated.
title: ReversingLabs: BubbleLoader turns WinRAR and other programs into malware carriers

validation.note: ReversingLabs original (highlights and intro read; full body only summarised) and Help Net Security's detailed write-up, which restates the vendor research.

review.note: Compared with ReversingLabs (Nov 17) and Help Net Security: entry-point patch, two PNGs, hosts, per-run hash change, Feb 2026 samples, Sept/Oct clusters, delivery unstated.
